title: Catalog ingest acceptance slate and pinning boundary definition
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Clarify requirements and acceptance criteria for ingesting new open model weights into the Model Catalog. This ticket captures the scope for metadata required at intake, the allowed pinning semantics (hard pin / soft pin / unpinned), required compatibility signals from runtime and tooling, and explicit fallback behavior for unpinned or incompatible variants. The goal is to produce a minimal, machine-readable ingest contract that runtime engineers, model curators, and the onboarding automation can rely on to avoid unexpected runtime failures or silent quality regressions.
scope_changes: Initial PRD scoped only metadata fields; expanded to include explicit fallback behavior and rollout constraints after Eng review.
Added requirement for a lightweight automated runtime sanity probe that runs at intake for unpinned variants.
Split acceptance criteria into 'ingest-time' and 'runtime-enforcement' buckets per feedback from SRE.
requirements_summary: Ingest manifest must include: model architecture tag, parameter count, expected tokenization spec, kv-cache compatibility flag, quantization tested profile (fp16/int8/etc), and provenance URL (weights + license).
Pinning semantics must be one of: 'hard-pin' (no auto-fallback), 'soft-pin' (preferred but fallback allowed), 'unpinned' (runtime selects compatible variant).

Compatibility signals required: max_context_length, kv_cache_supported (boolean), preferred_attention_kernel (string), recommended_batching_profile (latency/throughput), and known-incompatibilities list.
Unpinned variants must provide a recommended fallback variant key or a fallback policy tag (e.g., 'compatible-flan-variant' or 'runtime:pick-most-similar').
An automated runtime sanity probe must execute during ingestion for unpinned or soft-pinned variants and report perf/latency deviation and a small acceptance sample of generation quality metrics.
Ingest API should reject manifests missing required fields with clear error codes; warnings emitted for optional but strongly recommended signals (e.g., quantization profile).
acceptance_criteria: Given a manifest with all required fields, ingest API returns 200 and creates a catalog entry with pin_status set according to manifest; entry shows provenance URL in UI.
Given a manifest lacking required fields, ingest API returns a 4xx error with human-readable message listing missing keys and a machine-readable error code for automation retries.
For soft-pinned variants, the runtime fallback policy honors the 'recommended fallback variant key' and logs a fallback reason; metrics dashboard surfaces fallback frequency per variant.

The automated runtime sanity probe runs within the ingestion pipeline for unpinned or soft-pinned variants and produces a sanity report stored as an artifact (latency percentiles, sample outputs, numeric quality deltas).
There is a documented escalation path: entries failing sanity probes are flagged 'needs-review' and cannot be promoted to 'recommended' without manual sign-off from model-curation or runtime owners.
Console displays pin status and compatibility flags on the catalog entry; queries to the Catalog API include compatibility filters (e.g., kv_cache_supported=true).
A small integration test suite demonstrates fallback behavior across at least three runtime profiles (hosted, dedicated-gpu, private-vpc) using mocked requests.
risks: Incomplete compatibility signals may cause runtime to select a slower or incompatible kernel leading to latency SLO violations.
Overly strict hard-pin policy could block legitimate performance-improving fallbacks during outages.
Sanity probes may have false negatives on small sample sizes; risk of rejecting acceptable variants if thresholds are too tight.
dependencies: ENG-45781: catalog-api: ingest manifest validation and error codes
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Brief sync with runtime leads; agreed to require kv_cache_supported flag and a fallback_variant key for unpinned entries.
2025-02-18: PM/Eng trade-off: accept 'soft-pin' to balance safety and flexibility; runtime team to emit fallback telemetry for dashboarding.
2025-02-21: UX review: catalog UI will show a 'pin provenance' tooltip linking to the manifest provenance URL and the sanity probe report.
2025-02-25: Security review requested for provenance handling and signed manifests (see security_review_required).
